correctness.rationale: Fixed-point-freeness forces \(p\nmid m\), so the kernel module is semisimple. Kernel conjugacy classes are free \(C_m\)-orbits, while every coset \(Vh^j\), \(j\ne0\), is one conjugacy class because \(1-h^j\) is invertible. Kernel-kernel and outside-outside class pairs cannot be invariable generators. A mixed pair is adjacent exactly when \(\gcd(j,m)=1\) and the kernel representative is a cyclic module vector. For a commutative semisimple cyclic-group algebra, such a vector exists exactly when each irreducible constituent has multiplicity one, and then their number is \(\prod_i(p^{d_i}-1)\). The packaged exhaustive replay verifies every representative pair in five independent finite cases.

value.rationale: The primary source explicitly asks for connectivity of \(\Lambda^+(G)\) throughout the soluble invariably \(2\)-generated class. The theorem settles that question for a broad structural family of affine Frobenius groups, including reducible multiplicity-free kernels, and gives more than connectivity: an exact complete-bipartite graph and closed formulas for every active and isolated conjugacy class. The repeated-constituent obstruction also explains exactly when this family ceases to be invariably two-generated.
